Test Description: This testcase validates multi-channel transmit and receive operation on the DWC Ethernet QoS IP (Ethernet0) across all four DMA channels (CH0 through CH3). The test exercises the full MAC, MTL, and DMA subsystem configuration including MAC speed and duplex mode selection, MAC address programming, MTL TX/RX queue operation modes with quantum weight assignment, RX queue-to-DMA channel mapping, and per-channel DMA descriptor ring setup. TX and RX descriptors are preloaded for all four channels. The test sequentially activates each DMA channel starting from CH3 down to CH0, triggering the Ethernet VIP sequencer for each channel. Each channel is expected to transfer 10 packets, and cumulative TX/RX packet counts are validated at thresholds of 10, 20, 30, and 40 packets respectively. Conditional logic supports RX descriptor ring reload when the tail pointer reaches the end of the ring. The test completes after all four channels have been validated.
Test Steps / Procedure:
Step 1: Initialize the interrupt controller and enable all interrupts.
Step 2: Select the Ethernet interface based on the build configuration.
Step 3: Configure the MAC Configuration register for the desired speed and duplex mode (10M, 100M, or 1G; Full or Half Duplex).
Step 4: Configure MAC Extended Configuration, Packet Filter, RX Queue Control registers (Ctrl0, Ctrl1, Ctrl2), and VLAN Tag Control.
Step 5: Program MAC Address registers (Address0 through Address3, High and Low) for multi-channel address filtering.
Step 6: Mask MMC IPC RX interrupts via the MMC IPC RX Interrupt Mask register.
Step 7: Configure MTL Operation Mode and set TX Queue Operation Mode for all four queues (Q0-Q3). Assign quantum weights to each TX queue.
Step 8: Configure RX Queue Operation Mode for all four queues (Q0-Q3) and set RX Queue Control registers.
Step 9: Configure MTL Queue Interrupt Control Status for all four queues.
Step 10: Configure DMA Mode and DMA Channel Control for CH0.
Step 11: Set DMA TX Control and RX Control for all four channels (CH0-CH3).
Step 12: Program TX and RX Descriptor List Addresses for all four channels.
Step 13: Set TX Descriptor Ring Length and RX Control2 (RX descriptor ring length) for all four channels.
Step 14: Set TX Descriptor Tail Pointers for all four channels to initiate TX DMA.
Step 15: Enable DMA interrupts for all four channels via Interrupt Enable registers.
Step 16: Configure RX Queue-to-DMA Channel mapping via MTL RXQ DMA Map0 register and verify by reading back.
Step 17: Set RX Queue Control registers for all four queues.
Step 18: Preload TX descriptors for all four channels with packet data.
Step 19: Preload RX descriptors for all four channels.
Step 20: Configure power management register.
Step 21: Enable CH3 RX by updating DMA CH3 RX Control and setting CH3 RX Descriptor Tail Pointer. Trigger the Ethernet VIP sequencer.
Step 22: Poll RX and TX packet count registers. Monitor CH3 Current App RX Descriptor and RX Descriptor Tail Pointer; if the tail pointer reaches the end of the ring, conditionally reload RX descriptors and reset the tail pointer. Validate cumulative packet count reaches 10 TX and 10 RX.
Step 23: Enable CH2 by updating DMA CH2 TX Control, remapping RXQ DMA Map0, setting CH2 RX Descriptor Tail Pointer, and enabling CH2 RX Control. Trigger VIP sequencer.
Step 24: Poll and validate cumulative packet count reaches 20 TX and 20 RX. Monitor CH2 descriptor tail pointer for conditional reload.
Step 25: Enable CH1 by updating DMA CH1 TX Control, remapping RXQ DMA Map0, setting CH1 RX Descriptor Tail Pointer, and enabling CH1 RX Control. Trigger VIP sequencer.
Step 26: Poll and validate cumulative packet count reaches 30 TX and 30 RX. Monitor CH1 descriptor tail pointer for conditional reload.
Step 27: Enable CH0 by updating DMA CH0 TX Control, remapping RXQ DMA Map0, setting CH0 RX Descriptor Tail Pointer, and enabling CH0 RX Control. Trigger VIP sequencer.
Step 28: Poll and validate cumulative packet count reaches 40 TX and 40 RX. Monitor CH0 descriptor tail pointer for conditional reload.
Step 29: Update CH2 and CH3 TX Descriptor Tail Pointers for additional transfers.
Step 30: Wait for completion delay and finish the test.

Validation / Acceptance Criteria:
1. After CH3 activation and VIP sequencer trigger, the cumulative RX packet count must equal 10 and the cumulative TX packet count must equal 10.
2. After CH2 activation and VIP sequencer trigger, the cumulative RX packet count must equal 20 and the cumulative TX packet count must equal 20.
3. After CH1 activation and VIP sequencer trigger, the cumulative RX packet count must equal 30 and the cumulative TX packet count must equal 30.
4. After CH0 activation and VIP sequencer trigger, the cumulative RX packet count must equal 40 and the cumulative TX packet count must equal 40.
5. For each channel (CH3, CH2, CH1, CH0), when the RX Descriptor Tail Pointer matches the Current Application RX Descriptor and the tail pointer has reached the end of the descriptor ring, the RX descriptors must be conditionally reloaded and the tail pointer must be reset to the beginning of the ring.
6. The MTL RXQ DMA Map0 register must be readable and return the written mapping value upon readback verification.
7. The test must complete successfully by reaching the final completion step without hanging in any polling loop.
Remarks: The test supports multiple speed configurations (10M, 100M, 1G) and duplex modes (Full, Half) selectable via build-time configuration. The default configuration is 1G Full Duplex. An optional build configuration controls whether RX descriptors are reloaded when the descriptor ring is exhausted during polling. Ethernet interface selection is also configurable at build time. Channels are activated sequentially from CH3 to CH0, with the RXQ-to-DMA mapping updated before each channel activation. Each channel is expected to handle 10 packets, for a total of 40 packets across all four channels.
